findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: A food protection manager was not observed at the facility during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) was advised to either have another employee or all employees certified in food protection management. Ensure there is a certified food protection manager at the facility during all hours of food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT - An employee was observed changing task and not washing hands before putting on gloves. CORRECTED - The employee was instructed to wash hands by the inspector to prevent contamination of food. Ensure hands are washed when tasks are changed and before putting on gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1.The bottom of the front non-functional prep cooler was observed to have food debris accumulation. 
2. The top shelf for storing mushroom in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.
3. The wall above the top shelf for storing mushroom in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.
4. The fan blade cover and fan casing in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.

The PIC was instructed to have the surfaces mentioned above, cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The pipe beneath the handwashing sink in the back area was observed to be leaking and temporarily repaired with duct tape. The PIC was informed that duct tape is not an approved material for permanent repairs in a food establishment as it is not smooth or easily cleanable. The PIC was advised to have the pipe properly repaired and the duct tape removed. Ensure the plumbing is maintained in good repair by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas in the facility were observed to be in need of cove tiles replacements:
1. THIRD REPEAT -  The left side of under the handwashing sink at the back area.
2. The right side of under the three-compartment sink.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the missing wall cove tiles in the areas mentioned above are replaced for smooth and easy cleaning.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.16(B)  Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The wall above the prep sink on the can opener table was observed to have soil accumulation. The PIC was informed. Ensure the wall is cleaned to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
An employee handling food was observed to not have a food handlers’ certificate. The PIC was instructed to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing in between tasks. Education was carried out and PIC was made aware about washing hands before donning gloves.  Ensure that hands are washed properly before donning gloves when switching in between tasks.  

When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.14 Inspector observed the accumulation of mold and soil in the ventilation duct above the dry storage area. PIC was made aware of the mold buildup. PIC ensured inspector that the duct would be clean appropriately. Ensure that the vent duct is monitored and clean at a regular frequency to avoid contamination of foods items. 

Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Inspector observed a piece of cove base to the left of the hand sink in back to be puloing away from the wall. Repair or replace this piece of cove base.
Inspector also observed the silicone caulk seal behind the 3 part sink to be dark with soil. Some of the seal is missing. Clean and replace the caulk seal. Maintain this seal clean and intact.

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Facility is currently without test strips to measure sanitizer. Provide test strips. Test strips will be here in two days according to the owner.

findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The three part sink has a caulk seal that is soiled and in disrepair. Remove caulk seal and replace with smooth cleanable caulk line.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306.

Observed multiple dented cans on the dry storage shelf. Ensure not to accept dented cans when receiving food inventory. Discussed with PIC.
